status: proposal working rubric; freeze with the team before final evaluation

roles.name: Traditional goalkeeper
roles.definition: Prioritises goal protection with relatively limited sweeping and build-up involvement.
roles.evidence_cues: Review starting depth and involvement across phases; save percentage alone describes performance.

examples.title: Gianluigi Buffon
examples.context: Juventus; a role emphasis, not his whole career
examples.description: Buffon recalls Juventus asking him to concentrate on saves rather than his more adventurous play at Parma.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The keeper stays behind a compact defence, deals with crosses, then kicks long instead of joining short build-up.

roles.name: Sweeper keeper
roles.definition: Leaves the goal area to defend space behind the defensive line.
roles.evidence_cues: Check repeated positioning and interventions beyond the penalty area.

examples.title: Manuel Neuer
examples.description: His interventions well outside the penalty area illustrate protecting the space behind a high defence.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: A through ball beats the centre-backs; the keeper races beyond the box to clear before the striker arrives.

roles.name: Distribution keeper
roles.definition: Participates regularly in building attacks through passing.
roles.evidence_cues: Review receiving options, pressure and pass destinations; retain a separate sweeping trait.

examples.title: Ederson
examples.description: His short and long passing makes the goalkeeper an active route for progressing possession.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The keeper receives a back-pass, draws a forward towards him and finds the free midfielder beyond the press.

roles.name: Ball-playing centre-back
roles.definition: Progresses attacks from defence with passes or carries.
roles.evidence_cues: Check line-breaking actions and possession context, not just total completed passes.

examples.title: Leonardo Bonucci
examples.description: His passes from central defence towards the wings and runners behind the opposition illustrate progression from the back.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: A centre-back carries past the first presser, then passes through midfield to a teammate between the lines.

roles.name: Stopper
roles.definition: Steps out from the defensive line to confront receivers early.
roles.evidence_cues: Compare challenge timing and position with the covering defenders.

examples.title: Sergio Ramos
examples.description: His aggressive advances from the back line to engage receivers illustrate the stopper behaviour.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: As a striker receives to feet, one centre-back steps forward to challenge while the other protects the space behind.

roles.name: Cover defender
roles.definition: Protects space behind a teammate who engages the attacker.
roles.evidence_cues: Review recovery movement and defensive relationships over repeated sequences.

examples.title: Sergio Ramos
examples.description: The same analysis describes Ramos covering when his partner is better placed to challenge; the phase changes the role.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: A teammate steps out to tackle; the covering defender drops diagonally to intercept the pass behind that teammate.

roles.name: Sweeper or libero
roles.definition: Acts as a spare defender behind the line; a libero may advance in possession.
roles.evidence_cues: Confirm the spare-player structure, then record forward carries separately.

examples.title: Franz Beckenbauer
examples.description: He operated as a free defender and could move forward to influence attacks.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The spare defender starts behind two markers, collects a loose ball and carries into midfield when space opens.

roles.name: Wide centre-back
roles.definition: Defends an outside channel within a back three and supports progression.
roles.evidence_cues: Verify the back-three role and cover behind the wing-back.

examples.title: César Azpilicueta
examples.description: His advances from an outside centre-back position illustrate how this role can support wide attacks.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The right centre-back covers behind the wing-back, then steps into the outside channel to support an attack.

roles.name: Defensive full-back
roles.definition: Maintains deeper wide cover and advances relatively selectively.
roles.evidence_cues: Compare position across sustained team possessions and defensive transitions.

examples.title: César Azpilicueta
examples.description: His comparatively restrained right-back role balanced a more attacking left flank; this is a style comparison.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The left-back advances while the right-back stays alongside the centre-backs to protect against a counter-attack.

roles.name: Overlapping full-back
roles.definition: Advances outside the wide attacker to provide width.
roles.evidence_cues: Review repeated outside runs, receptions and deliveries.

examples.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold
examples.description: He initially supplied an outside attacking route from right-back before taking on more central duties.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The winger comes inside with the ball; the full-back runs beyond him along the touchline to receive and cross.

roles.name: Underlapping full-back
roles.definition: Attacks the inside channel while a teammate supplies the width.
roles.evidence_cues: Track runs inside the winger and their destinations near the box.

examples.title: Conor Bradley
examples.context: Liverpool; runs beside a wide winger
examples.description: When the winger holds his width, Bradley can delay his run and attack the channel inside him.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The winger stays on the touchline; the full-back runs between the opposing full-back and centre-back for a through ball.

roles.name: Inverted full-back
roles.definition: Moves from the wide defensive line into central midfield in possession.
roles.evidence_cues: Confirm repeated central occupation and the return to wide defensive duties.

examples.title: Philipp Lahm
examples.description: Moving from right-back into midfield gave his teammates another central passing option.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: During build-up the right-back joins the holding midfielder centrally, then returns to right-back when the team defends.

roles.name: Attacking wing-back
roles.definition: Provides high width from the flank of a back-three structure.
roles.evidence_cues: Review the defensive back five and attacking wide coverage.

examples.title: Victor Moses
examples.description: His conversion from winger to wing-back illustrates providing attacking width with a back three behind him.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The wing-back advances outside a narrow forward to cross, then recovers into a back five when possession is lost.

roles.name: Inverted wing-back
roles.definition: Moves centrally in possession from a wing-back starting role.
roles.evidence_cues: Confirm both the wing-back base and recurring midfield involvement.

examples.title: Build-up from a back five
examples.context: Illustrative sequence; no fixed player comparison
examples.description: A wing-back leaves the flank to receive beside the pivot while a teammate maintains attacking width.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: After possession is lost, the same player returns outside the three centre-backs. Confirm that starting back-five structure before using this label.

roles.name: Holding midfielder or anchor
roles.definition: Protects the central area ahead of the defence and supports circulation.
roles.evidence_cues: Check screening, positional restraint and cover during teammates' attacks.

examples.title: Sergio Busquets
examples.description: He protected the centre-backs while teammates advanced and offered a safe return pass.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: Both number eights join the attack; the pivot stays central, screens the striker and recycles a backward pass.

roles.name: Ball-winner or destroyer
roles.definition: Seeks to disrupt opposition possession through challenges and pressure.
roles.evidence_cues: Review challenge intent, pressing and recovery context; separate attempts from successful tackles.

examples.title: N’Golo Kanté
examples.description: His tackling and interceptions near the box illustrate the ball-winning trait within a broader midfield role.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The midfielder closes down a receiver, contests possession and immediately pressures the next opponent if the first challenge fails.

roles.name: Regista or deep-lying playmaker
roles.definition: Directs build-up from deep midfield through receiving and distribution.
roles.evidence_cues: Review access to the ball, progression and switches; high pass volume alone is insufficient.

examples.title: Andrea Pirlo
examples.description: His deep receiving positions and range of distribution illustrate directing attacks from the base of midfield.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The pivot repeatedly receives from the centre-backs, changes the tempo and switches play to an unmarked winger.

roles.name: Half-back
roles.definition: Drops from midfield into the defensive line during build-up.
roles.evidence_cues: Verify repeated movement relative to centre-backs and return into midfield.

examples.title: Sergio Busquets
examples.description: Dropping between Piqué and Lenglet allowed the full-backs to advance during build-up.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The defensive midfielder drops between two spreading centre-backs to form a temporary three, then steps back into midfield.

roles.name: Segundo volante
roles.definition: Advances from a double pivot while a partner supplies cover.
roles.evidence_cues: Check the deeper starting pair and recurring forward arrivals.

examples.title: Leon Goretzka
examples.context: Bayern under Flick; double-pivot attacking runs
examples.description: His forward runs from beside Thiago illustrate the advancing member of a deeper midfield pair.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: One pivot remains behind the ball while his partner runs beyond the number 10 and arrives late in the box.

roles.name: Box-to-box midfielder
roles.definition: Repeatedly supports attacking and defensive phases across substantial depth.
roles.evidence_cues: Review forward arrivals and defensive recovery; distance alone is insufficient.

examples.title: Jordan Henderson
examples.description: His attacking support and recovery work illustrate repeated involvement at both ends of midfield.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The midfielder supports a cutback near the opposition box, then tracks a runner back towards his own penalty area.

roles.name: Mezzala
roles.definition: Moves from central midfield into attacking half-spaces and wide combinations.
roles.evidence_cues: Check starting midfield role, creative involvement and side-channel movement.

examples.title: Kevin De Bruyne
examples.description: His movement into the inside-right channel to create crossing opportunities illustrates this midfield role.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: Starting beside a deeper pivot, the midfielder drifts outside the opposing central midfielder and combines with the winger.

roles.name: Carrilero
roles.definition: Shuttles laterally to connect play and protect a flank.
roles.evidence_cues: Review balancing movement and cover around the wide defender.

examples.title: Jordan Henderson
examples.description: His lateral support and protection of the right flank provide a comparison for the shuttling trait.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The right-sided midfielder slides towards the touchline to link play, then covers the space vacated by the full-back.

roles.name: Free number eight
roles.definition: Roams from central midfield to support creation in varying zones.
roles.evidence_cues: Check repeated rotations and reception zones across phases.

examples.title: Luka Modrić
examples.description: His movement to connect teammates across the pitch illustrates the roaming and creative elements of this working label.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The midfielder receives on one side, rotates through the centre and supports another combination on the opposite side.

roles.name: Attacking number eight
roles.definition: Advances from midfield to support the attack and arrive near goal.
roles.evidence_cues: Compare forward arrivals with the player's midfield starting position.

examples.title: Frank Lampard
examples.description: A recognised number eight whose forward involvement is a useful reference for assessing runs from midfield.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The midfielder starts behind the forwards, delays his run and reaches the penalty spot just as a cutback arrives.

roles.name: Advanced playmaker
roles.definition: Creates chances from spaces behind the main striker.
roles.evidence_cues: Review between-line receptions and passes that enable attacking opportunities.

examples.title: Mesut Özil
examples.description: His preference for receiving between the lines and supplying teammates illustrates an advanced creator.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The number 10 receives behind the opposition midfield, turns and slips a pass through for the striker.

roles.name: Trequartista
roles.definition: Roams between midfield and attack with creative freedom and usually lighter defensive duties.
roles.evidence_cues: Review roaming and defensive participation; a central attacking heatmap is insufficient.

examples.title: Francesco Totti
examples.description: Creative freedom let him roam between the lines, into the half-spaces and deeper to connect attacks.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The creator leaves his central starting area to find an unmarked pocket while other teammates maintain the defensive structure.

roles.name: Enganche
roles.definition: Acts as a relatively fixed advanced passing hub.
roles.evidence_cues: Compare stable reception zones and teammates' movement around the hub.

examples.title: Juan Román Riquelme
examples.description: Boca used him as their creative reference point; compare his passing-hub behaviour rather than labelling every movement.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The playmaker stays in a central pocket and receives repeatedly while forwards and wide players make runs around him.

roles.name: Shadow striker
roles.definition: Attacks scoring areas from a position behind the centre-forward.
roles.evidence_cues: Review runs beyond the striker and box arrivals, not goals alone.

examples.title: Dele Alli
examples.description: Runs beyond Kane from the attacking midfield line illustrate attacking scoring space from behind a striker.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The striker drops towards the ball; the number 10 accelerates past him into the space between the centre-backs.

roles.name: Traditional winger
roles.definition: Supplies touchline width and attacks outside to deliver.
roles.evidence_cues: Review wide receptions, outside progression and delivery locations.

examples.title: Antonio Valencia
examples.description: Touchline running and crosses for Rooney illustrate his earlier winger role.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The winger receives wide, beats the full-back on the outside and crosses rather than moving into central shooting space.

roles.name: Inverted winger
roles.definition: Receives wide and commonly moves inside onto the stronger foot.
roles.evidence_cues: Check footedness and repeated ball-carrying direction.

examples.title: Arjen Robben
examples.context: Bayern Munich; cutting inside from the right
examples.description: His inside-forward play provides a comparison for the specific trait of moving infield onto his left foot.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: A left-footed right winger receives near the touchline, carries inside and opens a shooting or passing angle.

roles.name: Inside forward
roles.definition: Moves from a wide starting position into central scoring areas.
roles.evidence_cues: Review diagonal off-ball runs and box occupation.

examples.title: Mohamed Salah
examples.description: His runs from the right towards central defenders and shooting positions illustrate a wide scorer.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: As the striker comes short, the wide forward runs diagonally behind the defence and receives close to goal.

roles.name: Wide playmaker
roles.definition: Creates passing opportunities from a wide or half-space base.
roles.evidence_cues: Compare creative distributions with touchline running and crossing.

examples.title: Hakim Ziyech
examples.description: Moving inside from the right gave him opportunities to create with through balls and deliveries.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The wide player receives in a half-space, pauses for runners and threads a pass rather than immediately attacking the byline.

roles.name: Pressing winger
roles.definition: Helps direct opposition build-up through wide pressing duties.
roles.evidence_cues: Review pressure timing and blocked passing lanes.

examples.title: Kingsley Coman and Serge Gnabry
examples.description: Their pressure on Chelsea’s outside centre-backs illustrates coordinated pressing from the wings.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The winger curves his approach to close the full-back while blocking the pass inside, helping trap possession near the touchline.

roles.name: Raumdeuter
roles.definition: Finds attacking space through well-timed movement from a flexible base.
roles.evidence_cues: Review repeated unmarked arrivals relative to defenders; touches alone are inadequate.

examples.title: Thomas Müller
examples.description: His elusive movement into unoccupied spaces illustrates finding opportunities without needing long dribbles.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The attacker waits outside a defender’s view, then moves into the gap created when that defender follows a teammate.

roles.name: Poacher
roles.definition: Focuses on finding and finishing chances near goal.
roles.evidence_cues: Review box movement and shot locations relative to build-up involvement.

examples.title: Javier Hernández
examples.description: His specialist goalscoring role illustrates the poacher comparison.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The striker stays near the centre-backs, darts across the near post and finishes a low cross with one touch.

roles.name: Target man
roles.definition: Serves as a receiving outlet who secures possession and involves teammates.
roles.evidence_cues: Review contested receptions, hold-up sequences and lay-offs; height alone is insufficient.

examples.title: Olivier Giroud
examples.description: Receiving direct passes and connecting with Hazard provided an outlet beyond Swansea’s midfield.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The forward controls a long pass under pressure, shields it and lays it off to a supporting midfielder.

roles.name: False nine
roles.definition: Drops from the striker line to create an extra midfield option and space for runners.
roles.evidence_cues: Observe the vacated space, defensive responses and teammates' runs.

examples.title: Lionel Messi
examples.description: Dropping from the central forward position created midfield options and space for other attackers.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The nominal striker drops between the lines; a centre-back follows, and a winger attacks the vacated central space.

roles.name: Deep-lying forward
roles.definition: Drops to connect midfield and attack while retaining a forward role.
roles.evidence_cues: Review link play and the surrounding striker structure.

examples.title: Harry Kane
examples.description: Coming towards the ball helped connect play while Alli, Son and Lamela ran beyond him.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: A forward drops to receive, lays the ball off and supports the next attack while a partner keeps the defence occupied.

roles.name: Advanced or channel-running forward
roles.definition: Threatens space behind the defence from a high starting position.
roles.evidence_cues: Review run origins, depth and channel destinations. This is a project working label.

examples.title: Timo Werner
examples.description: His pace and movement towards wider spaces stretched defenders and threatened the space behind them.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: Starting on the last defender’s shoulder, the striker bends his run into the gap between the centre-back and full-back.

roles.name: Pressing forward
roles.definition: Leads pressure on the opposition's first build-up line.
roles.evidence_cues: Review pressing triggers, angles and supported team pressure.

examples.title: Yussuf Poulsen
examples.description: His work at the front of Leipzig’s press illustrates a striker contributing to regaining possession.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The striker presses a centre-back on a backward pass, blocks the pivot and directs play towards the team’s pressing trap.

roles.name: Second striker
roles.definition: Works off a leading striker to combine and attack space.
roles.evidence_cues: Confirm the partnership and recurring position relative to its leader.

examples.title: Eden Hazard
examples.description: Playing off Giroud, he offered combinations and carried forward into spaces around the leading striker.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: The main striker occupies the centre-backs; his partner receives a lay-off and attacks the gap beside him.

roles.name: Complete forward
roles.definition: Combines several forward behaviours across different situations.
roles.evidence_cues: Require repeated evidence of linking, receiving, running and finishing involvement; defer a standalone class.

examples.title: Robert Lewandowski
examples.description: Finishing in varied ways and dropping to link attacks illustrate several forward behaviours in one player.

examples.title: What it looks like
examples.description: Across separate sequences the forward holds up a direct pass, links a combination, runs behind and attacks a cross. One action is insufficient.

pilot.note: Planning heuristics, not a sample-size guarantee. Complete forward remains descriptive.

examples_note: Player comparisons illustrate selected behaviours in the stated context, not permanent labels. Illustrative sequences are teaching examples, not verified events in the selected footage.
